# QM2025 A4 v1

Template ID: `qm2025-a4-40-8-6`; version 1. Source supplied by the user: `QM 2025 - A4 - Ky kiem tra - O ghi diem.pdf`. Archived at `docs/references/templates/qm2025-a4-v1.pdf`; SHA-256 `ABCB092FC9349290DAAF58D6EFE9748F3412524D3E2124023DED3883A773BC3B`.

This one-page 595x842 PDF contains text/vector geometry rather than an embedded page image. The PNG reference is rendered at 2x. This specific variant has a six-column SBD region (optionally used according to the selected key), three-column code region, 40 ABCD questions in four ten-question columns, eight True/False questions with four ideas each, and six numeric questions with four printed columns. Do not infer compatibility from the QM brand name; alternate layouts need separate geometry/versioning.

The canonical frame is 1053x1485 pixels, based on the four outer marker centers at approximately PDF (34.16,49.74), (560.54,49.74), (560.54,792.06), (34.16,792.06). Additional interior markers fingerprint and validate all three regions. Full capture and live preview use the same geometry. Alignment uses an outer projective transform plus a fixed triangular mesh of local marker residuals for gently curved paper (build 27). The source-specific pixel/point coordinates are in QmSheetGeometry. Density is measured locally in circle centers against the aligned blank reference; printed digits sit outside the code circles.

Raw reading slots are 0-39 for Part I, 40-47 for Part II, 48-53 for Part III. A selected key maps only enabled/configured slots into compact stored responses. Never truncate the first N raw slots for mixed parts. T/F idea tokens are T/F, underscore (blank), X (multiple), and question mark (uncertain); a pending idea blocks confirmation. Resolved partial questions preserve all four tokens and score by the number of correct ideas, even if another idea is blank/multiple. Numeric columns allow minus only in the first column, comma only in the two middle columns and digits in all four. Trim unfilled leading/trailing slots; internal gaps or malformed numbers require review. A multiple-filled numeric column makes that question invalid. Exact normalized decimal comparison handles comma/period, redundant zeroes and negative zero without floating tolerance.

Recognition fixtures are generated from the blank reference in tests, with marks across every answer block, code 209, decimal/sign/leading-empty-column examples, JPEG encoding, rotation, multiple marks and live probing. This is not evidence of measured accuracy on a printed/photographed QM sheet. Before calling the template calibrated, obtain phone photos with known keys/responses, including normal perspective, light shadows, faint pencil and erasures. No private photograph is bundled or uploaded.

Default scoring table follows the previously researched THPT 2025 structure, but the user can configure it for school tests: https://locthanhbaoloc.lamdong.edu.vn/home/uploads/news/2024_09/quyet-dinh-so-764_qd-bgddt.pdf . Point values are configuration, not properties inferred from the paper. Optional parts start disabled; Part I remains required.


## Candidate-number option (build 25)

The six x coordinates are PDF 432.02, 442.58, 453.02, 463.58, 474.02, 484.58; row y is 115.86 + 14.88 * digit. Apply the same canonical transform and baseline/local density classification as the three-digit code. Return six DigitReading values and a crop covering PDF x423/y108/width70/height151. Preserve leading zeroes and mark ambiguous columns with question marks instead of guessing. Raw readings are local/transient; the chosen key's scanCandidate flag controls whether they are shown, required and saved. Off keys record an unknown candidate even if the raw field was legible. Saved snapshots include the flag; old schema-6 configurations default off.

Regression coverage adds IDs 001286, 012345 and 678909; blank, faint and multiply filled columns; switch persistence; manual verification; selection between enabled/disabled codes; schema-6 migration, snapshot history and backup retention. These PDF-derived synthetic tests do not establish physical-photo accuracy.


## Physical-photo calibration (build 27)

Seven user-supplied physical photographs exposed two issues: smaller interior squares were rejected by the still-image minimum size, and an outer-corner homography displaced the dense code/candidate fields on curled paper. QM now accepts markers down to five pixels in the normalized still image, considers up to 60 components, and preserves the original four-corner plus eleven-interior-marker fingerprint. Sixteen additional controls improve the mesh when present; a missing optional control retains its projective position. Sampling never searches for the darkest nearby answer.

The fixed mesh follows the measured marker centers on both the photo and blank reference. Circle-core radius stays three pixels and classification thresholds remain unchanged. Background sampling moves from radii 8-10 to 12-14 pixels, beyond the larger Part I outlines; the old annulus could mistake an outline for a dark scene. Dark/faint/ambiguous marks still require review.

QM camera guides use 90% rather than 80% of the preview, and a complete detected sheet may extend beyond the suggested guide while remaining inside the actual preview with a 2% margin and minimum-size check. Keep the NTL guide policy unchanged. Tap-to-capture and the two-frame green-status rule remain.

All seven photos match the visually checked three-digit codes and all 54 raw response slots (only Part I was shaded). The six-digit candidate is clear on six photos; one retains a genuinely ambiguous column for manual verification. All seven are detected by the 800-pixel live probe and fit the revised framing policy; a rotated/recompressed physical sample also passes. These photos do not validate physically shaded Parts II/III or the camera stream on every device. Synthetic multipart, faint/multiple, wrong-template and NTL regressions remain required. Private photographs stay in ignored test/fixtures/qm-real/, outside app assets and Git; optional regression tests skip when these local files are absent.
